findings.text: §17 says ambix's `imas_alambic.bundles` entry point will "offer every `maps/<machine>/` that holds a `bundle.json`", but `discover_bundles` loads one entry point target and accepts only a `MapBundle` (`declared.append(target)`) or a directory path (`roots.append(Path(target))`); a callable returning a collection falls to the `else` branch, so `Path(<tuple of bundles>)` raises `TypeError` before any bundle is read. The repo-root `maps/<machine>/` set is dynamic and gitignored, so it cannot be registered as one static entry point per machine, and the engine's entry-point contract has no iterable form — yet §17's write-path list names no engine file (`machine_map.py` is absent), so the mechanism the section describes cannot work as written.

findings.reason: the section's third call site is in an ambix file its write paths do not grant, so the plan must add `imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py` to the write paths (or drop the claim of "the two" sites and justify leaving the third).
findings.text: §16 states that "the two store-root lookups that drop it" are `MachineMapCatalog.description_store_root_path` (`packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/machine_map.py:1230`) and `load_machine_map` (`machine_map.py:1404`), but the census of `resolve_store_root` call sites that omit `search_path` is three, not two: `_resolve_store_addressing` in `imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py:213` also calls `resolve_store_root(catalog.description_store_root, kind="description store")` with no `search_path`, so it falls back to `resolve_settings().maps` and the `IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH` environment variable. Because `imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py` is outside §16's declared write paths, a `write --maps <bundle>` with `IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH` unset still fails its description-store lookup after the two named edits land.

findings.text: §18 adds a `maps pull <machine>` subcommand that fetches a tagged bundle from `ghcr.io/simon-mcintosh/imas-alambic-<machine>`, but the same operation already has an owner: `imasdb.sh:70` does `gh auth token | oras pull --username "$GH_USER" --password-stdin "$BUNDLE_REF" -o "$BUNDLE"`, and the section touches `imasdb.sh` only to say it "defaults to the latest stable tag and no longer names a date". Two independent oras-pull paths would then exist over the same registry and the same gh token, and a change to either (auth form, artifact type, digest verification) drifts from the other.
